programs.name: Pretrial Assessment and Release Supervision (PARS)
programs.summary: Pretrial release program. OC Probation's site calls it the 'Pretrial Assessment Release Service Program' and lists the PARS unit at (714) 569-2000. County agenda documents describe it as a Court–Probation partnership (pilot began 2016): the court's Pretrial Services Officers interview and score in-custody defendants with the VPRAI risk tool, Probation prepares the risk report/recommendation for the judge, and people released onto PARS are monitored by Probation based on their risk score and the judge's specific orders, with progress and non-compliance reports to the court. Exact check-in method and frequency depend on your release order — read it and ask your PARS officer. Probation will not give case-specific info by email.
programs.todo: Court/Probation role details come from an OC agenda PDF (ocagendaext.oc.gov/ExtDocViewer/746a3af1-...) whose text was not machine-verified; Probation's PARS page itself gives no description. Typical check-in conditions (phone/office/EM) not published — not filled in.

programs.name: Adult Drug Court
programs.summary: Voluntary, 5-phase program of at least 18 months: supervision, counseling, drug testing and regular court appearances for seriously addicted, high-risk/high-need offenders. Partners: Probation, Health Care Agency, PD, DA, Sheriff. Held at Community Court (Thursdays 8 a.m. per court page).

programs.name: DUI Court
programs.summary: For repeat DUI offenders: felony cases at least 18 months/5 phases; 2nd- and 3rd-time misdemeanor cases at least 12 months/3 phases. Partners include Probation, HCA, PD, DA, Sheriff, MADD.

programs.name: Veterans Treatment Court
programs.summary: 5-phase program of at least 18 months for justice-involved veterans/military needing mental health treatment (e.g., PTSD, TBI). VA case manager, Probation high-control supervision; HCA for vets not eligible for VA services. Community Court, Tuesdays 1:30 p.m. per court page.

programs.name: Military Diversion (PC 1001.80)
programs.summary: Pre-plea diversion up to 2 years for current/former U.S. military members with service-related conditions (PTSD, TBI, substance use, etc.); assessment from VA, HCA or other agency required; charges dismissed on successful completion. Heard in Dept. C46. Coordinator: MDmotions@occourts.org.

programs.name: Whatever It Takes (WIT) Court
programs.summary: Voluntary program of at least 18 months for offenders with chronic, persistent mental illness (schizophrenia, bipolar, major depressive disorder) who are homeless or at risk; counseling, psychiatric care, housing, peer mentoring. Community Court, Mondays 9 a.m. per court page.

programs.name: Recovery Court
programs.summary: Voluntary 5-phase program of at least 18 months for offenders with chronic and persistent mental illness; Probation supervision plus HCA PACT or other treatment.

programs.name: Opportunity Court (Co-Occurring Disorders)
programs.summary: Voluntary 5-phase program of at least 18 months on the Drug Court model for offenders diagnosed with schizophrenia, bipolar disorder or major depressive disorder.

programs.name: Assisted Intervention (AI) Court
programs.summary: Voluntary program of at least 18 months with immediate treatment for offenders with severe and persistent mental health diagnoses and lower criminogenic risk.

programs.name: Homeless Outreach Court
programs.summary: Resolves outstanding infractions, quality-of-life misdemeanors and warrants for homeless individuals while connecting them to housing and health services. Community Court, Wednesdays 3 p.m. per court page.

programs.name: Young Adult Court
programs.summary: For defendants ages 18–25 charged with an eligible felony who meet program criteria; alternating Fridays in Dept. C1, Central Justice Center. Referrals by email (YAC@occourts.onmicrosoft.com).

programs.name: Prop 36 Treatment Program
programs.summary: Court-supervised substance use treatment (case management, drug testing, progress reviews) for people charged with certain drug possession offenses.

programs.name: Mental Health Diversion (PC 1001.36)
programs.summary: Pre-plea diversion for defendants with a mental health disorder diagnosed or treated within the last 5 years. Defendant pleads not guilty, waives time and files a motion with a proposed treatment plan. Treatment up to 1 year (misdemeanor) or 2 years (felony); charges dismissed on satisfactory completion. Coordinator: MentalHealthDiversion@occourts.org.

programs.name: PC 1000 Drug Diversion
programs.summary: The court's Alcohol and Drug Program page lists 'PC1000 Providers' (Orange County Health Care Agency provider list) — i.e., the court may order a PC 1000 drug program. The page itself does not describe eligibility; ask your attorney whether PC 1000 applies to your charge.
programs.todo: No OC-specific page describing PC 1000 eligibility/process found; statute text on leginfo returned 403

programs.name: Misdemeanor Diversion (PC 1001.95)
programs.summary: State law (effective Jan 1, 2021) lets a judge offer diversion on many misdemeanors, even over the prosecutor's objection. In Orange County, the published appellate decision Grassi v. Superior Court (2021) held DUI defendants are NOT eligible (Vehicle Code 23640); the CA Supreme Court denied review in 2022.
programs.todo: No occourts.org page on PC 1001.95 procedure found; source is the OC DA press release (prosecution framing). Statute text on leginfo returned 403 — not independently loaded.
